chunks: Abu Talib Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah ibn Banan Al-Ta’ee narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mansoor ibn Abdul Razzaq saying:

To the ruler of Toos, known as Al-Biwardi: 'Do you have any children?' He replied, 'No.' Then Abu Mansoor asked him, 'Why don’t you go to the Shrine of Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) and pray to God near him until He grants you a son? For I have asked God the Exalted for many of my needs there, and they were fulfilled for me.' The ruler said, 'I set out for the Shrine - may peace be upon its resident - and prayed to God the Exalted near Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) that He grant me a son. Then God the Mighty, the Exalted granted me a son. Then I came to Abu Mansoor ibn Abdul Razzaq and informed him that God the Exalted had answered my prayer in the Shrine. So he favored me, gave to me, and honored me for that.'

The author of this book (may God have mercy on him) said: When I asked the blessed Amir, Rukn al-Dawla, for permission to visit the Shrine of Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him), he granted me permission in the month of Rajab of the year 352 A.H. When I left, he called me back and said to me: 'This is a blessed Shrine which I have visited. I asked God the Exalted for needs that were in my heart, and He fulfilled them for me. So do not neglect praying for me there and visiting on my behalf, for indeed prayer there is answered.' I promised him that and fulfilled it. When I returned from the Shrine - may greetings and peace be upon its resident - and entered to see him, he said to me: 'Did you pray for us and visit on our behalf?' I said: 'Yes.' He said to me: 'You have done well. It has been proven to me that prayer in that Shrine is answered.'

key_terms.الْبِيوَرْدِيُّ: Al-Biwardi, a title/name of the ruler of Toos
key_terms.رُكْنَ الدَّوْلَةِ: Rukn al-Dawla, a title of the Amir (ruler)
key_terms.مَشْهَدُ الرِّضَا: The Shrine of Ar-Ridha (Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the Shrine of Imam Ar-Ridha for fulfilling prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual efficacy of the Imam's shrine in Tus, illustrating how intercession and supplication at the burial place of the eighth Imam can fulfill specific worldly needs, such as progeny. The text underscores the continuity of this practice through the author's personal experience with the ruler Rukn al-Dawla, reinforcing the shrine's status as a locus of divine acceptance (*maqbul al-du'a*) in Shia devotional tradition.
